AGENDA
  YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Tuesday, February 23, 2021
  6:30 P.M.
  The three-fold mission of the Youth & Family Action Committee is:
  1. To support positive activities and opportunities for young people;
  2. To strengthen families; and
  3. To combat the problems of substance abuse.

Tonight’s meeting will be held virtually in compliance with Governor Newson’s Executive
Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. The meeting will be live streamed on
the La Verne You Tube channel at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream. To participate in the full
meeting and discussion, please email yfac@cityoflaverne.org to receive information on
how to register.

To make a comment on an agenda item or under public comment, email your phone
number to cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. This email address will be monitored live during the
meeting and interested parties will be called. Please be aware there is a delay in the live
stream service and any requests to speak should be submitted as soon as possible.

minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  February 23, 2021

1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present (virtually):

  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Chair – Mayor Pro Tem
  Rick Crosby, Vice Chair – Council Member
  Krista Chakman, BUSD Board Member
  Carolyn Cockrell, Roynon Elementary School Counselor
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Don Kendrick, Resident
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Kim Bressell, BUSD
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Robert Nishimura, LVPD
  Rachell Killackey, Resident
  Kailey Killackey, Resident
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Assoc.
  Elise Wallis, American Lung Assoc.
  Kimberly Luna, American Lung Assoc.
  Inesh Rathi, American Lung Assoc.
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Marissa Scholefield, David & Margaret
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the January 26, 2021, meeting were
  approved.

4. School Resource Officer  Administrative Lieutenant Sam Gonzalez with the
  police department noted that School Resource
  Officer (SRO) Janessa Gonzalez was unavailable
  and he would be reporting for the evening. Sam
  shared that the police department was making
  preparations for students to be back on campuses
  including bringing back crossing guards for the
  elementary schools. Sam also reported that SRO
  Gonzalez would be brought back from patrol duties
  and back on campus within the next few weeks.

5. Tobacco Enforcement  TECO Officer Robert Nishimura with the police
  department provided an overview of tobacco
  enforcement efforts supported by a grant through the
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes February 23, 2021, page 2

  Department of Justice. Efforts have included visits to
  the skate park to speak with community youth,
  attendance at school registration events with the
  paraphernalia board, and updating the municipal
  code to better enforce things like vaping in
  parks/schools. Additionally, Robert noted
  enforcement visits to all retailers that carry tobacco
  and tobacco related products at least 2 times
  recently.

6. American Lung Association  Jessica Vozella with the American Lung Association
  facilitated a presentation regarding the Healthy Lungs
  La Verne initiative. Jessica as well as other
  representatives of the American Lung Association
  shared information on steps their group has taken to
  educate the community on the dangers of flavored
  tobacco products and vaping products. They also
  shared information on engaging community groups
  on the issue as well as provided information on
  recommended actions and steps that other area
  cities have taken. The group provided support for
  revising the City’s Municipal Code to address the
  concerns presented by the American Lung
  Association and the Executive Committee directed
  staff to prepare a letter from YFAC requesting the
  City Council’s support for the revisions.

7. BUSD In-Class Return  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  shared the district has announced plans to open on
  campus learning for elementary students (includes 6th
  grade) based on state and county guidelines. The
  district will be sending out information along with a
  survey to effected parents to gauge interest and
  address potential concerns. Mark noted it will be a
  hybrid model of learning and additional planning is in
  process with additional specifics to come out in the
  following weeks.

  The group discussed optimism with the ability to get
  students back on campus along with sports and other
  extracurricular activities.

8. Public Comment  None

9. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for March 23rd
  at 6:30 p.m.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes February 23, 2021, page 3

10. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:35 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Assistant to the City Manager
